title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (inferred from pp. 76-79). This is Grothendieck's 1986 axiomatics of 'analysis situs'. M is a set of 'objects' (imaginaires) with relations: ≤; |○| ('étrangers', disjoint), whose negation is 'overlap'; and ||. For a family L of objects, supp°(L) is a closure: the set of Z in M such that every object étranger to L is étranger to Z. That is a biorthogonal or Galois closure for the orthogonality |○|. Σ_M is the set of 'constructible supports'. A 'support function' φ realises each object X as an open set |X|° of a space P, with |L|° = ∪_{X∈L}|X|°. 𝔉 is a distinguished class of families F. From context these are families of mutually étranger objects, a kind of 'partition' or 'test'. Full faithfulness relative to F (p.77) says: every point outside |F| lies in some |Z|° that misses |F|. The Proposition of p.77 then gives φ(supp°L) = |L|° for every L ⊂ F.

This page draws the consequences.

Corollary 1: the map L ↦ supp°(L), from P(F) to Σ_M, preserves:
- non-empty intersections;
- arbitrary unions, where the union goes to the sup in Σ_M;
- relative complements: for L ⊂ Ψ ⊂ F, supp°(Ψ∖L) = supp°Ψ ∩ ∁supp°L.

Corollary 2: the image Σ_{M,F} of P(F) is the set of constructible supports 'subordinated to F'. It is stable in Σ_M under finite non-empty inf, under sup, and under relative complement A∩∁B. The realisation A ↦ |A|° = ∪_{X∈A}|X|° maps Σ_{M,F} into P(|F|) ⊂ P(P) and commutes with these operations. In other words, Σ_{M,F} is a Boolean algebra, a homomorphic copy of P(F), realised by honest open subsets.

Terminology: a family of constructible supports is 'admissible' if there is some F ∈ 𝔉 to which all of them are subordinated.

Scholie (continued on p.79): on admissible families the operations sup, inf and relative complement obey the usual set-theoretic laws. Examples are distributivity and A∖(A∖B) = B. Also A∩B = ∅ ⟺ A|○|B. So 'all pathology disappears'.

Purpose. The global lattice Σ_M of supports is non-distributive and pathological. Grothendieck isolates 'compatible' families, those refined by a common orthogonal family F, on which a genuine Boolean calculus of supports holds. This prepares the 'axiome des supports' on p.79.
errors: Read literally, with ∁ the set-theoretic complement in M, the relative-complement formula of Corollary 1 is false. Take Ψ = F and an object Z ∈ supp°F that overlaps both members of L and members of F∖L. Then Z lies neither in supp°L nor in supp°(F∖L), yet it does lie in supp°F ∩ ∁supp°L. The formula holds after applying φ, i.e. |Ψ|°∖|L|° = |Ψ∖L|°, using disjointness of the |X|° for X ∈ F. At the level of supports, ∁ must be read as an orthocomplement or cosupport. This is exactly how the 'axiome des supports' on the next page is formulated: supp°(F) ∩ cosupp°Φ = supp°(F∖Φ). So the corollary as written anticipates an axiom rather than following from the Proposition.

Commutation with intersections, supp°(∩L_i) = ∩supp°(L_i), tacitly needs the members of F to be pairwise étranger, i.e. the |X|° pairwise disjoint. Otherwise an intersection of unions is not the union of the intersection. This hypothesis is presumably built into the definition of 𝔉 but is not restated.

Commutation with intersections is asserted in Σ_M, but the proof only gives equality after applying φ. Lifting it back requires that φ be injective (faithful) on supports. The page does not justify this; p.77 notes that 'the property implies faithfulness' only in a marginal remark.

ideas.what: Support of a family as the biorthogonal (Galois) closure for an orthogonality/disjointness relation; the lattice Σ_M of closed supports
ideas.modern_name: Ortholattice of biorthogonally closed sets of an orthogonality space (Dacey space); Galois connection closure
ideas.usually_credited_to: Birkhoff (polarities, 1940); Dacey (1968), Foulis-Randall (1970s) for orthogonality spaces

ideas.what: Boolean sub-algebra of the support lattice generated by subsets of one orthogonal family F, mapped homomorphically onto open sets ∪|X|°
ideas.modern_name: Boolean subalgebra generated by a test / maximal orthogonal set; 'events of a test' in a Foulis-Randall test space
ideas.usually_credited_to: Foulis and Randall (test spaces, operational logic, 1970s)

ideas.what: Admissible (= jointly subordinated to a common F) families of supports, on which distributivity and the set-theoretic laws hold
ideas.modern_name: Compatible / commeasurable elements of an orthomodular lattice or orthoalgebra, which generate Boolean blocks
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quantum logic: Birkhoff-von Neumann (1936), Kalmbach, Foulis-Randall

ideas.what: Realisation of abstract supports by open sets of a space via a fully faithful support function
ideas.modern_name: Representation of a lattice of regions by regular-open / open sets (point-free topology, mereotopology)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Stone, Tarski, de Laguna/Whitehead tradition; locale theory
ideas.where_published: Possibly echoed in Récoltes et Semailles remarks on 'topologie sans points'; unsure

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 1986 support calculus has the structure of a Foulis-Randall test space / orthoalgebra. Objects play the role of outcomes, |○| is orthogonality, the families F ∈ 𝔉 are tests, and supp° is biorthogonal closure. His 'admissible families' play the role of compatible events forming Boolean blocks. His observation that 'all pathology disappears' on admissible families is the standard phenomenon that compatible elements behave Booleanly. This link between his mereotopological 'analysis situs' and quantum logic does not appear to be in the literature.
missed.quote: Pour les familles admissibles de supports constructibles, les opérations Sup, Inf, complémentaire relatif — et donc les bonnes propriétés ensemblistes habituelles … toute pathologie disparaît.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Results on orthoalgebras and test spaces could directly answer his open questions on p.79. These include whether a faithful support function that is not fully faithful exists, and what the role of the 'axiome des supports' is, which resembles orthomodularity/coherence. The link would also give his unpublished axiomatics a recognisable modern home.

missed.claim: The programme of an axiomatic, point-free 'analysis situs' built from disjointness and support relations was never completed or published. This page is one step: Boolean behaviour on admissible families, as a prelude to the support axiom.
missed.quote: Terminologie Une famille de supports constructibles (dans F) dite "admissibles", s'il existe F ∈ 𝔉, tels qu'il soient tous subordonnés à F.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is relevant to mereotopology and point-free topology, and to Grothendieck's tame-topology vision in the Esquisse. Its exact axioms are not documented elsewhere.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is elementary lattice theory. Its interest lies in the unpublished framework and in the striking, apparently unnoticed parallel with Foulis-Randall test spaces and compatibility in orthomodular lattices.
transcription_corrections: The archive folio number '87' in the bottom-left corner is omitted.
In Corollary 1, '∁' is written as a complement sign applied to supp°L. Given the next page, it may stand for cosupp (orthocomplement) rather than the set complement.
In 'stable dans Σ_M', the handwritten insertion reads 'au Σ_M' / 'dans Σ_M' above 'par inf'; the meaning is unchanged.
The struck-out line reads 'l'image de 𝔓(F) dans Σ_M'. The inserted replacement is 'subordonnés à F'.
